title: Recycle handoff at the WCLI-39 / WCLI-35 boundary
description: A recycle handoff written and discharged in one session, at opum-agent's renewal order on 2026-09-29, after WCLI-39 landed and was promoted and before WCLI-35 starts. It carries WCLI-35's measurement, mechanism, fix design, scratch copies and the intended branch name, so the successor re-derives none of it. Read THIS record first; it points at the work.
implementationNotes:
RECYCLE HANDOFF, 2026-09-29, written at opum-agent's recycle order and discharged in-session (the WCLI-40 shape). The successor's next task is WCLI-35; everything below was measured this session in scratch copies, and the repository is clean.

STATE, VERIFIED AT THIS WRITE. origin/main = origin/dev = acf7e9f1eddb74f77e292c1b71ac79a3c7d12ea5 (WCLI-39 merged as opum-ai/ward-cli#78 and promoted via opum-ai/ward-cli#79). WCLI-39 is Done, record in .quest/completed/. WCLI-35 is To Do with its original description and acceptance criteria; it was briefly claimed this session and the claim was reverted on the recycle order, so it starts clean. No task is In Progress. Local branches are dev and main only; tree clean. Read WCLI-39's completed record for the binding-rule consolidation that just landed, and WCLI-35 for the task itself.

WCLI-35 — CORRECTED SCOPE (opum-agent accepted). Fix TWO sites in src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts: create's pre-lock layoutOf check, and mutate's pre-lock requireVault. read needs NOTHING: its requireVault already sits inside db.transaction(() => ...).deferred(), a one-snapshot read, and header() already wraps its layout read the same way. Do not claim a read fix; record read as verified already-safe.

MECHANISM, instrumented rather than inferred. layoutOf is three reads — PRAGMA application_id, PRAGMA user_version, SELECT type, name, tbl_name, sql FROM sqlite_schema — taken as separate statements outside any transaction, so they can observe the file at three different moments. A concurrent create whose commit lands between them hands back a state that never existed (its vault table present, its header fields not yet); layoutOf classifies that as neither empty nor ward and refuses with vault_store_unrecognized, where the contract is vault_exists. Every instrumented failure carried the same tag: WARD-DEBUG layoutOf id=0 version=0|1 schema=1. A two-connection experiment reproduces the mixed read exactly when the commit lands between the reads, and shows the commit cannot land inside a read transaction: the writer waits, or gets SQLITE_BUSY when it has no busy timeout.

THE FIX, ALREADY WRITTEN AND VERIFIED IN SCRATCH. /tmp/ward-fix/pending/sqlite-vault-store.ts and /tmp/ward-fix/pending/vault-store.test.ts are the exact working-tree versions from this session: a settledLayout(db) helper — db.transaction(() => layoutOf(db)).deferred() — plus requireSettledVault(db), the same one-snapshot reading of requireVault's answer. create calls settledLayout for its pre-lock check; mutate calls requireSettledVault; the in-transaction checks keep plain layoutOf. The test file adds one case, "a commit can land between bare reads and cannot land inside a read transaction", pinning the premise the fix rests on (bare reads interleave a commit; a read transaction cannot), in the file's existing two-connection style; note it needs mkdirSync(directory, { mode: 0o700 }) because fresh() does not create .ward. With those two files copied over the repository's, test/vault-store.test.ts passes 40/40 (39 pre-existing plus the new case) and typecheck is clean.

SCRATCH COPIES, which survive the recycle. /tmp/ward-repro — the pre-fix copy, carrying WARD-DEBUG logs on the four vault_store_unrecognized throw sites in src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts; repro.ts races two create processes (bun repro.ts <n>); race-read.ts races a creator against a reader or mutator (bun race-read.ts read|mutate <n>, mode-tagged summary); worker.ts and reader-worker.ts are the two halves. /tmp/ward-fix — the same scripts against a fixed copy (the earlier variant of the fix; pending/ above is the current one). Both run entirely in temporary directories with a synthetic key.

COUNTS. create vs create: 3 mismatches in 3000 pre-fix (earlier runs 1/400 and 3/1200), 0 in 3000 post-fix. mutate vs create: 3 in 2500 pre-fix; read vs create: 0 in 1500 pre-fix, consistent with read's check already being inside a deferred transaction. Post-fix: read 0/2500 and mutate 0/2500. Per-mode pre-fix rerun: read 0/1500, mutate 0/1500 — the window is roughly 0.1 percent per iteration, so a no-hit rerun is expected and does not contradict the 3/2500. Store tests: 39/39 on the fixed copy, 40/40 on the branch working tree.
